ELITE.compositionNote: Elite Pools & Unified Portfolios continue to draw on PIMCO, Loomis Sayles and iAGAM as sub-advisors. The one confirmed structural change this year remains at iAGAM itself: the Asset Allocation team that steers strategic/tactical tilts across these pools is now led by Tej Rai and Alex Bellefleur following Sébastien Mc Mahon's move to Chief Economist, iA Financial Group. iA Clarington also continues to expand its broader active shelf (e.g., the Jul 27/26 International Multifactor Equity Fund launch), though no change to the Elite Portfolios' own strategic allocation targets was found as of today. An advisor quick-reference guide (investia.ca) shows illustrative underlying sub-fund weights for at least one Elite Pool (Loomis U.S. All Cap Growth ~25%, QV Global Equity ~10%, BMO MSCI EAFE Index ETF ~15%, Capital Group Global Equity Canada ~20%), but which specific pool this applies to was not confirmed today — cite only as illustrative of the shelf's multi-manager structure, not as a named pool's current allocation. This week's sharply escalated Iran war (IRGC missiles at a US carrier, the US destroying or disabling three more Iranian tankers) and the BoJ's hardened hike signal (see CCM5604) remain the most relevant live macro test for the fixed-income sub-advisors inside these pools; PIMCO continues to frame such shocks within its 'Fragmentation Era' thesis, but neither PIMCO nor Loomis Sayles has issued a note specifically reacting to this week's missile-and-tanker escalation yet.
